name: validation-tier-planner-identity
title: Add stable validation command identity and an explain-only Story-relevance validation planner
description:
Implements Rollout Story 1 of docs/requirements/decisions/story-relevance-dynamic-validation-tiers-execution-plan.md (authored under Story B-ccf4). That file is not present on main; it currently exists on branch story/B-ccf4, which is verifiable with `git show main:docs/requirements/decisions/story-relevance-dynamic-validation-tiers-execution-plan.md` failing while `git show story/B-ccf4:<same path>` succeeds.

Today `proof-or-stop validate` either runs the whole configured command inventory or filters it by the static `focus` tag in `filterFocusedConfiguredCommands` (packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts). There is no Story-derived relevance, no stable per-command identity, and no way to explain why a command would be run. Adding more static focus tags would create a second hand-maintained test matrix that drifts.

This Story adds ONLY the foundation the plan calls Story 1: a stable command id plus a normalized command-set digest, a canonical legacy pin resolver, a Story input collector built on the existing rename-aware/freshness readers, language-neutral planner types with the fail-closed widening matrix, and a read-only `validation_plan` CLI that explains the plan. It performs NO relevance pruning: every request that would need an impact or exclusion decision reports effective tier repository-full or a classified stop. No lifecycle gate, no routine validation reuse rule, and no DONE-required evidence path changes. Static impact graph, worktree overlay projection, exclusion proofs, runner decomposition, tier execution, and shadow recall belong to Stories 2-4 and are explicitly out of scope.

Development follows RED then GREEN: each behavior lands as a failing fixture first, then the implementation that turns it green.
